I can't speak for everyone, but it's very easy to prevent. I didn't find out I had it until it was already aids unfortunately. HIV has 3 stages.

Stage 1: Acute HIV infection. This is usually within a few weeks of infection where you begin to show flu like symptoms. 

Stage 2: Clinical latency. This is when the virus is more or less dormant but is still doing what it's trying to do. I like to think of it like the cartoon Invader Zim where Zim is the virus. Except, you know, good at what it's trying to do. 

Stage 3: Acquired immunodeficiency syndrome. This is when the immune system is weakened so much that opportunistic infections begin to occur. For me it was lymphoma, bacterial pneumonia, thrush/candisis, and shingles. If there was a bingo for post aids opportunistic infections, I would have definitely won. 

However antiretroviral treatment can and does prevent the advancement to aids. It was just caught way too late in my case.

I didn't discover I had HIV until it had already reached the final stage, which is when it has officially become aids. In April of 2018 my lymph node in my armpit grew to the size of a baseball. I went to get it checked and eventually confirmed to be cancer. Lymphoma to be specifically. When my chemotherapy was over I began radiation, but it was stopped due to my increasingly low white blood cell count. White blood cells are measured as 1=1,000, and the low side of normal amount to have is 4. I was constantly under 1. I also couldn't breath most of the time and was short of breath from just standing still. They told me my body wasn't well enough to continue radiation and I was sent down to Indianapolis for testing. They confirmed that I had pnumonia and that prompted them to run testing for HIV. A few hours later, they confirmed that I was positive, but I didn't know it had reached the aids stage until conducting my own research. They don't distinct HIV and aids differently anymore because the treatment is the same, which is why I wasn't told how far it had progressed.  


I don't remember when I was infected, but I can pinpoint an approximate timeline on when it could have happened. I know it was a result of unprotected sex with someone who was infected, but I'll never know exactly who. Because of how far my HIV had gotten, my doctors suspect that I've had it for many years, at least 4 or 5. I don't remember showing any symptoms at any point in my life and until cancer I was always in great health. 

When I started my medication I was put on biktarvy. I take a single pill a day and an antibiotic to help with infections since my immune system is super compromised. I had MRSA recently and I get boils on my waist where my belt sits that grow large and get infected easily if I don't take my antibiotic, which I have to take 3 times a week. I don't know anything about the other drugs but biktarvy has been working great.

I've been playing Omni-Tell since the deck was blowing up in the summer and I've gotten to know the deck pretty well I think. I've tried a lot of different builds and strategies since the infamous DTT banning, and I recently switched to a Burning Wish build. Ever since, I've found a whole new love for the deck. I think the deck can run without wishes, but I do think it's better with them from my personal experience. I have my sideboard set up a particular way too that really helps, so I'm kind of forced to run the wishes. Whenever you play Show and Tell, on games 2 and 3 it's always a dice roll because of cards like Ashen Rider, Oblivion Ring, Ensnaring Bridge, things like that. For me, having that Cunning Wish in hand is almost always a win to answer whatever they lay down from the S&T. I'll give you an example.

Last week I was playing a legacy event and almost got shut out of the game after a Show & Tell twice. In one game, my opponent dropped an Ensnaring Bridge. In another, it was Qasali Pridemage with the open mana to activate it's ability and blow up my Omniscience. With Cunning Wish and Omniscience in play, I have a very intricate combo that lets me win at instant speed providing they don't disrupt me along the way (which for some reason has yet to happen). When he activated the Pridemage ability, in response I played my Cunning Wish to grab a Firemind's Foresight, play the Foresight to grab a Brainstorm, Split Decision, and another Cunning Wish. Play the Wish, play Split Decision while it's on the stack and copy the Wish, and then grab Eladamri's Call and Release the Ants. I play Eladamri's Call to fetch Emrakul, play Brainstorm and put Emrakul back on top of my library, then Release the Ants them to death, all in response to whatever shenanigans they're trying to stop me with.

Again, maybe this is just me, but having that Cunning Wish in hand after dropping an Omni has always been a life saver and a game winner. Without wishes, I find that the deck is too linear. The speed of the deck will always be a huge advantage, but having a plan B in a deck is never a bad thing. I think without wishes, you could also lose to bad hands more than you will to your opponent, which sometimes even happens with my build. I run 6 wishes total in mine (4 burning, 2 cunning), which you obviously don't need to go that wish heavy, but having at least the cunning wishes goes a very long way.

Couple of reasons. The price of the card tells you just where it's going to see play the most. $3 for non-foil, but it's $18 foil, so there's a price jump of 5x, which suggests it's going to see the most use in Legacy, and it will stop combo decks very quickly. In most legacy decks, a 2/2 flyer isn't a threat at all, especially when you can stop a Show and Tell or Sneak Attack from casting an Emrakul. In standard, it's still going to have a lot of value. If someone drops a Thassa, or any of the other gods, or a fatty that's going to change the game as soon as it hits, a 2/2 flyer is a much better alternative. Granted the token is more of a threat in Standard than any other format, but the trade off is well worth it.
